extraction.retrieval_anchor: Markdown inventory document 123, world laws 31-60 and system axes
extraction.notes: World laws 31-60 plus document-level design axes extracted individually; design claims remain UNVERIFIED.

claims.normalized_claim: Cleaning should be a mechanic that can reveal secrets or remove evidence.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Surfaces can carry a readable alphabet or rune system whose appearance depends on environmental state.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Local gravity or reality weight can be represented visibly through particle and motion behavior.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Biome boundaries should form mixed transition zones rather than abrupt invisible borders.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: A map can itself be a shader-affected world object that becomes wet, smears or reveals details under conditions.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Fire aftermath should progress through ash, embers, smoke and later soil or vegetation consequences.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Fog should act as an information filter that changes silhouettes, visibility and moisture.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Starlight and moonlight should alter edges, plants and puzzle-relevant states.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Clouds can act as moving rule zones that carry shadow and interrupt systems such as solar input.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Unnaturally perfect cleanliness can itself be a clue that a place or illusion is false.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Heat distortion should be a geometry-affecting state that can warp air, wood, metal, glass and ropes and thereby alter mechanics.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Drying should serve as a visible clock through changing puddles, footprints, blood and clothing.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Smoke should stratify under ceilings, move through openings, react to temperature and reveal airflow.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Breath should act as a truth indicator for cold, fear, poison, disease or invisibility.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Touch should leave persistent traces such as polished handles, dust-free lids and worn edges that support forensic reading.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Social warmth should make inhabited, abandoned, grieving or celebratory spaces visibly different.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Lies can be represented as material inconsistencies such as wrong shadows, delayed reflections or implausible dust.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Guilt can remain visibly attached through persistent blood, soot, shadow or animal reactions.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Blessing and curse can be expressed through altered surface behavior such as rot, moisture, dew or rune visibility.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: World fatigue can flatten color, slow particles, damp sound, droop plants and weaken fire.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Over-care or excessive cleanliness can act as a warning sign of artificiality.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Magic should leave material memory such as mineralization, brittleness, magnetization, moss growth or pigment bleaching.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Habitual routes should physically emerge over time as grass paths, worn market areas, patrol routes or animal tracks.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Animal fear zones should make nearby wildlife react to otherwise hidden threats.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Metal should carry history through blood sheen, impact heat, polishing, rust and crack-dependent sound.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Food should behave as world state through drying, insects, bruising, steam and visible poisoning cues.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Language can leave visible world-state traces such as dustfall, smoke changes, reflection errors, calmed particles or startled birds.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Proximity should age materials through nearby fire, water, magic, crowds or corpses.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Boundaries should be visible as physical tension expressed through dust, snow, light, vegetation or traffic patterns.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: Major consequences should leave long-lived scars such as burn recovery, battlefield wear, flood lines, drought cracking or regrowth.
claims.subject: world-law

claims.normalized_claim: The document is a long-term design reference and is not part of the binding current roadmap.
claims.subject: vision-weltgesetze

claims.normalized_claim: Every visible state should have at least one gameplay consequence, with no purely decorative effect and no invisible state without a visual trace.
claims.subject: world-law-design

claims.normalized_claim: Every shader or world state should have an explicit lifetime ranging from seconds to permanent scars.
claims.subject: world-state

claims.normalized_claim: World states should be transferable between entities and media, for example mud on boots, smell on clothing, blood in water and smoke in wind.
claims.subject: world-state

claims.normalized_claim: Every effect should support three readability levels: atmospheric, interpretable and mechanically actionable.
claims.subject: world-state

claims.normalized_claim: Every visible problem should have at least one countermeasure or player action that can respond to it.
claims.subject: world-state

claims.normalized_claim: The preferred first proof level combines snow, footprints, wind, blood and torchlight because it connects several visible-state systems at once.
claims.subject: prototype

claims.normalized_claim: The document claims SHADED already provides foundations for wind, water flow, season migration, day-night material behavior, fog, cold or frost and material fatigue.
claims.subject: SHADED

claims.normalized_claim: The document claims trail-texture work forms a foundation for footprints, dirt, fire aftermath and blood-as-information systems.
claims.subject: SHADED
